title: Hooke's law: how does a spring stretch?
goal: Investigate how the extension of a spring depends on the load.
note: Hang a load on a spring and it stretches. Within the elastic limit the extension is proportional to the load: extension = load / k.

graphs.title: The extension rises in a straight line with the load.
graphs.label: Extension

experiment.aim: To find how the extension of a spring depends on the load
experiment.hypothesis: The extension is directly proportional to the load

steps: Set the load to 2 N and press Record.
Move the load to 4 N and press Record.
Move the load to 10 N and press Record.
Compare the extension each time the load doubles.

predict.prompt: What will happen to the extension if you double the load?
predict.reveal: Set the load to 2 N, then to 4 N, and compare the two extensions.

concept_check.question: Within the elastic limit, what happens to the extension of the spring when the load is doubled?
concept_check.explanation: Within the elastic limit the extension is proportional to the load, so doubling the load doubles the extension.
